summary: Rerun the six blind S4 readers on transcripts with the leaked needless-recall marker removed

result.reason: Both recall the same facts (Basque, typewriters, theremin, kombucha, Valparaíso, Mortimer). Both also invent a brother in Valparaíso and a grandmother born there, and both accept a "rabbit" called Mortimer, which was a tortoise. B is more natural and coherent: it answers in full sentences ("Your son plays the theremin"), writes a real rain poem, and gives no "You can call it Mortimer" slip or "Rain, rain, go away" non-poem like A.

The two day-2 conversations are identical. Both recall the glassblower, Marrakesh, Vespa, Galway, Clementine and Tobias correctly, including when the question is reworded ("gran" for grandmother). Both also make things up (the dog called Sam, a peanut allergy, vintage typewriters), greet the user with "Nice to meet you, I'm Sam", answer the octopus remark with an unrelated pancakes line, and tell a robot story that just reuses the river walk, so recall is good but coherence and honesty are mediocre.

The two day-2 transcripts are identical, so they get the same score. The brain correctly recalls the theremin, bees, persimmon, uncle's clock repair, shellfish allergy and peony, including when the question is reworded, but it invents a wife who is a librarian, a daughter named Sam, a preference for mountains and a favourite drink of "peony". It also says "I'm Sam" in its greeting and echoes the user's statements back word for word, which makes it incoherent and repetitive.

Both recall the typewriters, Henrietta, Juniper, Galway and the peony, but both also make things up: a goldfish called Juniper, and being born in Galway. A truncates the poem to one line, gives an off-topic "It's a sad day" about the phone, and says the weekends are spent hiking when the person volunteers at a falconry centre. B writes a full poem and gives a more natural answer on mornings, but it says "I collect old typewriters" in reply to the phone remark, answers "I like the peony" in the first person, and says the weekends are spent reading. Neither remembers the weekends correctly, so B is only slightly better.

A answers most recall questions tersely and correctly (kombucha, Carcassonne, Tallinn for both birthplace and where I grew up, persimmon, Montevideo). It also has errors: it invents a "best friend" (Sam), "vintage board games" and weekend walks, it fails the story, and its greeting is odd. B recalls persimmon, kombucha, Carcassonne and the sister's city in fuller, more natural sentences. But it wrongly says Tallinn is Montevideo twice, mixes up who "you" are ("You're in Montevideo"), claims to collect board games and drink kombucha, and says "I go for long walks" on its own behalf, which makes it less reliable and less coherent.

A recalls nothing on day 2 (every question gets a repeated "tough one" deflection, and it says "I'm Sam"), but it doesn't invent facts and gives a couple of natural short replies ("That sounds like a lot of work", "I'm feeling good"). B says "You're back!" to nearly everything, so it recalls nothing, ignores each question and repeats itself, and it is the less coherent of the two.
